question: Why is it so important for community nurses to connect families with respite care?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for insurance
options.B: To give caregivers temporary relief and prevent burnout
options.C: To punish families who fail to give medications on time
options.D: To permanently remove the client from the family home

explanation: Brilliant! Respite care gives hardworking families a much-needed break so they can recharge and stay healthy too.

question: Which common, lightweight device uses two small prongs to deliver low-flow oxygen right into a patient's nostrils?

options.A: Non-rebreather mask
options.B: Venturi mask
options.C: Nasal cannula
options.D: Simple face mask

explanation: You'll see nasal cannulas everywhere in the ward! They're the standard, comfortable choice for giving patients a little extra oxygen through their nose.

question: Why do youth health programmes include counseling against substance abuse?

options.A: Substance use is a legal matter handled exclusively by police officers.
options.B: Alcohol and drugs are only used by teenagers.
options.C: Lifestyle habits formed during youth heavily influence long-term health outcomes.
options.D: It is a requirement to receive government funding for equipment.

explanation: Spot on! Habits picked up in the teenage years often stick around. Catching substance use early helps prevent lifelong health struggles.

question: What do we call an infection that a patient picks up while receiving care in a hospital?

options.A: An allergic reaction to medication given during a surgical procedure
options.B: A chronic disease that worsens over many years of outpatient visits
options.C: Any illness a person brings into the hospital from their home environment
options.D: An infection a patient catches while inside a medical facility for care

explanation: You got it! These are known as healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), meaning they weren't there when the patient first arrived.

question: What usually happens when the delicate hormonal balance of the female reproductive system is disrupted?

options.A: Secondary sex characteristics reverse themselves instantly
options.B: Estrogen production permanently stops across all age groups
options.C: The reproductive organs immediately undergo complete atrophy
options.D: It can lead to issues ranging from irregular periods to more serious health concerns

explanation: Think of hormones like a delicate chain reaction! When one part is out of balance, it can throw off the whole cycle, leading to skipped periods or other reproductive challenges.

question: When you thoroughly wash your hands between patients in the ward, what are you mainly stopping?

options.A: It increases the resistance of the susceptible host.
options.B: It blocks the mode of transmission.
options.C: It destroys the natural reservoir of the pathogen.
options.D: It alters the portal of entry on the patient's skin.

explanation: Handwashing is your superpower! By washing your hands, you stop germs from hitching a ride from one patient to the next (blocking transmission).

question: Which type of bedpan is best to use for a patient who has a broken hip?

options.A: A standard high-backed bedpan
options.B: A rigid plastic commode chair
options.C: A fracture pan
options.D: A pediatric incontinence ring

explanation: Fracture pans are shallow, meaning you don't have to lift the patient's hips high up. This is a lifesaver for avoiding extra pain or injury when dealing with hip or pelvic bones!

question: In many poor communities, what is the main dietary cause of micronutrient deficiencies?

options.A: High intake of dairy products and fresh vegetables
options.B: Frequent eating of high-protein animal meals
options.C: Heavy reliance on a single starchy staple food
options.D: Excessive consumption of imported canned foods

explanation: Correct! Eating only one starchy food day in and day out means the body misses out on the wide variety of nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which type of longitudinal study follows the exact same specific individuals over time?

options.A: Panel study
options.B: Cross-sectional study
options.C: Pilot study
options.D: Trend study

explanation: Exactly! A panel study keeps track of the exact same set of participants across multiple visits.

question: What is the best way to organize the body of a literature review?

options.A: By the alphabetical order of the authors' first names
options.B: By the physical weight of the textbooks referenced
options.C: By the exact length of each published journal article
options.D: By themes, trends, or logical subtopics

explanation: Structuring your paper by themes lets you easily compare what different authors say about the same specific subtopic.

question: In a busy hospital, what percentage of the total waste produced is actually regular, non-hazardous household waste?

options.A: About 50%
options.B: About 99%
options.C: About 15%
options.D: About 85%

explanation: Most of what hospitals throw away is everyday rubbish (like paper and food packaging) that doesn't carry any infection risks. Only a small fraction is dangerous clinical waste!

question: Which lab test is the most reliable way to track declining kidney function?

options.A: Platelet aggregation rate
options.B: White blood cell count
options.C: Serum sodium concentration
options.D: Glomerular filtration rate

explanation: The GFR (Glomerular Filtration Rate) tells us directly how well the kidneys are cleaning the blood, making it the gold standard for checking kidney health.

question: Which blood test measures general inflammation by checking how fast red blood cells settle?

options.A: Liver function test
options.B: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.C: Complete blood cell count
options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

explanation: Often called ESR, this test watches how quickly red blood cells drop to the bottom of a test tube. Faster settling usually means high inflammation in the body.

question: Why do we routinely test the mother's urine for protein and acetone during active labour?

options.A: It proves whether the mother has taken her prescribed iron tablets
options.B: It helps identify pre-eclampsia and maternal starvation or dehydration
options.C: It measures the exact blood sugar level of the unborn baby
options.D: It determines the precise gestational age in weeks

explanation: Urine checks are quick lifesavers! Protein can point towards pre-eclampsia, while acetone tells you if the mother is running out of energy or getting dehydrated.

question: When we talk about 'local sources of nutrients' in Nigerian diets, what do we mainly mean?

options.A: Processed canned foods found in international supermarkets
options.B: Synthetic vitamins manufactured in laboratory settings
options.C: Foods grown and harvested within a community or country
options.D: Expensive dietary supplements imported from overseas

explanation: Spot on! Local nutrient sources are simply the foods naturally grown and produced right here in our environment or nation. It makes eating healthy much more practical!

question: When wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) during an outbreak, what is a common hazard nurses need to watch out for?

options.A: Contaminating oneself while taking off the gear incorrectly
options.B: Causing the laboratory printer to jam during data entry
options.C: Forgetting to check the expiration date on the patient's chart
options.D: Catching a cold from the air conditioning in the isolation room

explanation: You got it! Taking off (doffing) PPE the wrong way is one of the easiest ways healthcare workers accidentally contaminate themselves.

question: Why do we perform CPR on someone whose heart has stopped?

options.A: To cure the underlying cause of the heart attack
options.B: To clear any severe blockage in the upper airway
options.C: To maintain oxygenated blood flow to vital organs
options.D: To restore the normal rhythm of the heart immediately

explanation: Think of CPR as your hands acting as an artificial pump! It keeps fresh blood moving to the brain and heart until professional help or equipment arrives. You're keeping them going!

question: How do computers help nurses manage vital signs and patient numbers?

options.A: By following programmed steps to turn raw numbers into useful information
options.B: By making independent medical diagnoses using intuition
options.C: By storing information permanently without electricity
options.D: By turning handwritten notes into paper charts

explanation: Computers don't think like humans do! They rely on smart programming to turn raw numbers into clear, meaningful information for your shift.

question: Why must pit latrines be constructed a safe distance away from community drinking wells?

options.A: To prevent underground waste seepage from contaminating the drinking water
options.B: To ensure the toilets receive enough direct sunlight
options.C: To keep the water source smelling fresh and perfumed
options.D: To make it harder for children to play near the toilets

explanation: Locating latrines too close to water wells allows sewage to leak into the groundwater, causing widespread water-borne outbreaks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT part of an active drug history?

options.A: Past allergies or reactions to the substance
options.B: The dose and how often the drug is taken
options.C: The patient's childhood immunization record
options.D: The exact brand or generic name of the drug

explanation: Immunizations are part of the general medical history, not an active daily drug history. Every question you answer makes clinical practice clearer!

question: Which emotional response is most commonly seen in patients placed in strict isolation?

options.A: Relief and joy
options.B: Confusion about medication
options.C: Aggression and anger
options.D: Loneliness and anxiety

explanation: Physical separation from family and friends combined with masked staff often leaves isolated patients feeling lonely and anxious. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h7)

question: What does it mean for a nursing research project to show 'originality'?

options.A: Adding fresh insights or applying concepts in a new setting
options.B: Inventing a brand-new hospital building design
options.C: Writing a research paper without using any past references
options.D: Copying successful studies from foreign countries word-for-word

explanation: Well done! Originality means bringing a fresh perspective, new data, or trying an existing idea in a brand-new setting like our local Nigerian hospitals.

question: Which cells are the star players in our adaptive (targeted) immune response?

options.A: Adipocytes
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Lymphocytes
options.D: Erythrocytes

explanation: B cells and T cells are types of lymphocytes. They are the smart cells that handle the targeted, long-term memory side of immunity.

question: A patient taking a new medication for high blood pressure reports a sudden drop in sexual desire and function. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Sudden onset of an incurable neurological brain disorder
options.B: A completely normal result of eating a high-sodium diet
options.C: An infection caused by poor hand hygiene habits
options.D: Direct side effect of the prescribed antihypertensive drug

explanation: Certain blood pressure medications are well-known to interfere with sexual response and can cause unexpected dysfunction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h3)

question: Why did nurse leaders in the 1970s feel the need to build their own unique nursing theories?

options.A: To replace all medical textbooks with nursing journals
options.B: To prove that nurses were more important than physicians in hospitals
options.C: To better explain and guide the unique aspects of professional nursing care
options.D: To satisfy strict government tax requirements for universities

explanation: Think of it this way: borrowed theories couldn't fully capture what makes nursing special. Leaders needed original frameworks to truly guide everyday clinical practice.

question: What is the best way for a nurse manager to get staff to support financial goals?

options.A: Threaten workers with dismissal if supply costs go up by one percent
options.B: Involve frontline nurses in discussions and explain that financial health supports patient care
options.C: Keep all financial reports strictly secret from the nursing staff
options.D: Punish any nurse who asks questions about where unit funds are spent

explanation: When managers communicate openly, staff can see that managing money well actually protects the hospital's ability to help patients.

question: Which dimension of quality care ensures that clinical treatments are based on proven scientific guidelines?

options.A: Safety
options.B: Accessibility
options.C: Acceptability
options.D: Effectiveness

explanation: Brilliant! Effectiveness focuses on using evidence-based practices so that our nursing interventions actually achieve the best health outcomes for the patient.

question: What is the main goal of Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

options.A: Providing practical comfort, safety, and basic human support
options.B: Diagnosing personality disorders in disaster shelters
options.C: Prescribing psychiatric medications for long-term depression
options.D: Conducting deep psychoanalysis of childhood trauma history

explanation: You got it! PFA isn't heavy therapy. It's about being a comforting human presence, offering safety, and helping people meet their basic immediate needs. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary action a nurse should perform before preparing any medication?

options.A: Check the patient's room temperature
options.B: Ask the family member what drugs the patient takes
options.C: Verify the order against the medication administration record
options.D: Wash the medication trolley with bleach

explanation: Comparing the medication order against the official administration record prevents medication errors and ensures patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why do we need different sectors (like health, police, and fire) to work together during a major disaster?

options.A: Different agencies bring specialized skills, equipment, and resources that one group lacks
options.B: It prevents local volunteers from taking credit for successful rescues
options.C: It ensures that only the military makes medical decisions for victims
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pre-planning or emergency simulation drills

explanation: No single agency can do it all! Combining medical, security, and rescue teams ensures everyone gets the complete care they need. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h5)

question: What essential check must a nurse perform immediately after removing an IV catheter?

options.A: Rinse the puncture site with cold tap water
options.B: Measure the exact volume of blood left in the hub
options.C: Soak the removed plastic tubing in an antiseptic jar
options.D: Inspect the catheter tip to ensure it is fully intact

explanation: Checking the tip confirms that no broken plastic piece remains inside the patient's vein. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h9)

question: What type of molecule usually acts as a T-dependent antigen?

options.A: Water molecules
options.B: Plain lipids
options.C: Proteins
options.D: Simple salts

explanation: Proteins are complex structures that generally need help from T-helper cells to fully get the adaptive immune system working.

question: A nurse manager wants everyone on the ward to share ideas on a new admission form to get their support. Which style is she using?

options.A: Democratic
options.B: Transactional
options.C: Laissez-faire
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: That's democratic leadership! Involving the team makes everyone feel heard and willing to support the new change.

question: Why is early recognition of behaviour disorders so important in nursing care?

options.A: It prevents the behaviors from escalating into lifelong challenges
options.B: It immediately cures all family communication problems
options.C: It removes the need for any formal psychiatric evaluation
options.D: It guarantees that the child will never need medication

explanation: Catching these patterns early allows you as a nurse to help families intervene before actions severely damage a child's social and academic life. You've got this!

question: What are the coarse hairs located inside the nasal vestibule called?

options.A: Vibrissae
options.B: Turbinates
options.C: Cilia
options.D: Microvilli

explanation: Vibrissae are the stiff, coarse hairs at the entrance of the nose that catch large bugs, dust, and debris. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why do nurses pinch the skin when giving a subcutaneous injection to a slim patient?

options.A: To squeeze out trapped air bubbles inside the syringe
options.B: To speed up the absorption of the medication into blood
options.C: To lift the fatty tissue away from the underlying muscle
options.D: To numb the nerve endings near the injection site

explanation: Pinching gathers up that cozy layer of fat and safely lifts it away from the muscle underneath, ensuring your needle goes exactly where it's supposed to.

question: Which hormone causes the milk ejection reflex (let-down)?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Correct! Oxytocin is the 'let-down' hormone that makes the milk flow smoothly for your baby.

question: Why does batch cooking help save money?

options.A: It guarantees that food will never spoil under any condition
options.B: It requires buying expensive kitchen appliances upfront
options.C: It forces family members to eat less food overall
options.D: It reduces energy consumption and limits ingredient waste

explanation: Spot on! Cooking larger pots at once uses less cooking gas or kerosene and ensures ingredients get used up before going bad.

question: What is the best way to help prevent teenage pregnancies at the community level?

options.A: Mandatory curfews enforced by police officers
options.B: Banning teenagers from using public transportation
options.C: Comprehensive sexuality education and youth-friendly health services
options.D: Isolating pregnant teens from community activities

explanation: You nailed it! Giving young people clear health education and easy access to friendly, welcoming clinics helps them make safe choices.

question: What is the biggest safety hazard to watch out for during steam tent therapy?

options.A: Hypertensive crisis
options.B: Sudden hypoglycemia
options.C: Scald burns
options.D: Severe hypothermia

explanation: Correct! Because boiling water and hot steam are involved, burn prevention is always a top priority.

question: You need to collect a swab from a visible ulcer on the labia minora. What is the correct way to do it?

options.A: Scrape the lesion until it bleeds profusely to get cells
options.B: Press the swab deeply into the underlying muscle tissue
options.C: Rotate the swab firmly across the base of the ulcer
options.D: Rinse the ulcer thoroughly with sterile water first

explanation: Gently rotating the swab right at the base of the sore picks up the exact fluid and cells where the trouble-making germs are hiding.

question: In public health, what does disease 'eradication' mean?

options.A: Replacing all synthetic drugs with natural remedies
options.B: Treating all infected patients with herbal medicines
options.C: Worldwide reduction of the infection incidence to zero
options.D: Reduction of cases to zero in a single country only

explanation: Eradication means completely and permanently wiping out the germ and its reservoir everywhere on planet Earth. Gone for good!

question: Why does Addison's disease make a patient's skin turn a darker, bronze color?

options.A: Elevated levels of hormones that stimulate melanin production
options.B: Chronic dehydration leading to skin darkening
options.C: Increased exposure to sunlight caused by fatigue
options.D: Poor circulation trapping pigment in superficial capillaries

explanation: In Addison's, the brain pumps out extra signals to try and stimulate the adrenals; these hormones accidentally stimulate skin pigment (melanin) too, causing a dark tan look.

question: What is the main goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To replace family-based healthcare services completely
options.B: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff
options.C: To generate revenue for school infrastructure
options.D: To provide academic tutoring for struggling students

explanation: Spot on! The heart of any school health program is keeping everyone—both students and staff—physically, mentally, and socially safe and healthy.

question: If you gently scrape the creamy white patches of oral thrush on a patient's tongue, what do you usually see underneath?

options.A: Clear fluid blisters forming instantly
options.B: A bleeding, red base underneath
options.C: A completely normal, pale pink mucosa
options.D: Hard, calcified tooth enamel

explanation: Those white patches of thrush stick to an inflamed, raw surface that easily bleeds when scraped.

question: Before giving a drug, you use a bedside tool to scan both the patient's wristband and the medication. What is this safety tool called?

options.A: Automated vital sign tracking
options.B: Bar Code Medication Administration
options.C: Clinical Decision Support Systems
options.D: Electronic Health Record auditing

explanation: Brilliant! Bar Code Medication Administration (BCMA) is your trusty safety net at the bedside, making sure the right patient gets the right drug, dose, and route every single time.

question: What is the first step in the risk management process?

options.A: Patient discharge
options.B: Risk identification
options.C: Staff punishment
options.D: Financial compensation

explanation: You cannot manage a hazard until you first find out it exists by spotting it through reports, audits, or observation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of placing a stockinette under a cast?

options.A: To cure the underlying bone fracture quickly
options.B: To protect the skin from rough casting materials
options.C: To add extra weight to the broken limb
options.D: To make the cast dry much faster in the sun

explanation: The stockinette acts as a soft barrier preventing harsh plaster or fiberglass from rubbing directly against the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: What was the core belief of the Moral Treatment movement?

options.A: Mental illness should be met with kindness and a peaceful environment
options.B: Patients must be permanently separated from society
options.C: Strict physical punishment is necessary to cure madness
options.D: Spiritual exorcisms are the only true cure for mental disorders

explanation: Moral treatment shifted care away from cruelty and towards dignity, fresh air, useful work, and compassionate human interaction. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: How do immune system mix-ups usually cause skin disorders?

options.A: By increasing natural oil production until pores burst open permanently
options.B: By completely blocking blood supply to the outer layer of the epidermis
options.C: By attacking healthy skin proteins and triggering chronic inflammation
options.D: By preventing white blood cells from ever entering the dermal tissue

explanation: Exactly! Sometimes the immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks normal skin cells, leading to ongoing inflammation.

question: Which part of the heart forms the tip that hits the chest wall during a heartbeat?

options.A: The lower tip of the left ventricle
options.B: The middle wall dividing the ventricles
options.C: The upper base of the right atrium
options.D: The outer surface of the right atrium

explanation: The bottom tip (inferior tip) of the left ventricle makes up the apex of the heart that touches your stethoscope or fingers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why is the large surface area of the peritoneal cavity so useful in medical care?

options.A: It prevents any medication from entering the systemic bloodstream
options.B: It stores excess fat to protect organs from physical trauma
options.C: It completely stops bacteria from causing localized infections
options.D: It provides a wide space for efficient fluid and drug exchange

explanation: Exactly! Because the peritoneal membrane is so wide and full of tiny blood vessels, it acts like a giant sponge, making it easy to swap fluids and medicines in and out. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why is mouth care seen as a core nursing duty rather than just making a patient look neat?

options.A: Hospital rules state that nurses must inspect teeth every morning
options.B: Dentists are almost never found inside general hospital wards
options.C: The mouth is a main doorway for germs to enter the rest of the body
options.D: Being sick always makes patients completely lose their sense of taste

explanation: Spot on! The mouth opens directly into our breathing and digestive pipes, meaning good oral care protects the whole body, not just the teeth.

question: What assisted reproductive technique involves injecting a single sperm directly into an egg?

options.A: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection
options.B: Vasectomy reversal
options.C: In vitro fertilization
options.D: Intrauterine insemination

explanation: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) directly places one selected sperm into an egg to overcome severe male factor infertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h7)

question: Why do modern hospitals look at adverse events as system flaws instead of just blaming the nurse?

options.A: It allows management to fire careless staff members quickly
options.B: It proves that hospitals are entirely free from human error
options.C: It ensures that nurses never have to write incident reports
options.D: It helps shift the focus to fixing underlying broken processes

explanation: Spot on! When we fix the broken workflows and environment, we stop the same mistake from happening to another patient.

question: When does the diaphragm start moving back down to its usual position after birth?

options.A: Only when the mother starts breastfeeding
options.B: Six weeks after the baby is born
options.C: Immediately after the delivery of the placenta
options.D: Three months before labour begins

explanation: Once the baby and placenta are out, tummy crowding is instantly relieved and the diaphragm drops back down. Fantastic!

question: Which of these is a great example of a community-based preventive nursing strategy?

options.A: Punishing individuals who exhibit signs of mental distress
options.B: Waiting until a patient is in crisis before offering any help
options.C: School programs that teach children emotional regulation and coping skills
options.D: Closing local health clinics to save government funds

explanation: Prevention is key! Teaching kids how to handle emotions early on builds strong mental resilience before big problems start.

question: What ethical balance must nurses maintain while collecting data during a disaster?

options.A: Balancing hospital profits with the cost of medical textbooks
options.B: Balancing nursing working hours with physician holiday schedules
options.C: Balancing public health surveillance needs with patient privacy and confidentiality
options.D: Balancing local laws with international travel restrictions

explanation: Nurses must track outbreaks to protect the public while still respecting each patient's right to private medical information. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is a key benefit of presenting research at a scientific conference?

options.A: Guaranteeing automatic acceptance into international print magazines
options.B: Eliminating the need to ever write a formal research paper
options.C: Getting immediate feedback and networking with other professionals
options.D: Receiving a cash prize from the hospital management board

explanation: Conferences allow researchers to talk directly with peers, answer questions on the spot, and build useful professional relationships. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h3)

question: What complication happens if a localized lung infection spreads directly into the patient's bloodstream?

options.A: Sepsis
options.B: Pulmonary embolism
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary fibrosis

explanation: When germs escape the lungs and enter the general circulation, they can trigger a body-wide, dangerous inflammatory response known as sepsis.

question: A patient says they feel constantly terrified for no clear reason and cannot go to work. How should you as a nurse view this?

options.A: As a normal reaction to everyday life pressures that will resolve on its own
options.B: As a physical sign of a primary cardiac event rather than psychological distress
options.C: As an attention-seeking behavior requiring behavioral redirection
options.D: As an abnormal, pathological anxiety response that requires clinical evaluation

explanation: Great clinical thinking! When fear is constant, unprovoked, and stops someone from living their life, it goes way beyond normal worry and needs professional care.

question: Which nerve is most at risk when a gluteal (buttock) injection is given with poor technique?

options.A: Femoral nerve
options.B: Median nerve
options.C: Sciatic nerve
options.D: Radial nerve

explanation: Great nursing knowledge! The sciatic nerve runs deep in the lower buttock, so injections must be placed carefully in the upper outer quadrant to avoid it.

question: Why is calming a patient's emotions just as important as treating their physical wounds in a crisis?

options.A: It completely erases the memory of the traumatic event
options.B: It speeds up the hospital discharge process for all patients
options.C: It prevents the physical injuries from becoming infected
options.D: It lowers acute stress and supports physical healing

explanation: Great thinking! When we help patients calm down, their stress hormones drop, making it much easier for their bodies to heal and for them to work with us.

question: How should the nurse position the patient immediately after the thoracocentesis is finished?

options.A: Lying flat on the affected side with no pillows
options.B: Lying on the unaffected side for a short period
options.C: Flat on their stomach with arms raised over their head
options.D: Sitting upright with both arms locked behind the back

explanation: Positioning the patient on their un-punctured side promotes expansion and helps seal the puncture site. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h6)

question: An unconscious accident victim is brought in with heavy bleeding in their mouth. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Lay them flat on their back without neck support
options.B: Suction the airway while keeping the neck safely supported
options.C: Give oral pain meds to keep them calm
options.D: Send them straight for a chest X-ray

explanation: Brilliant! Clearing the mouth clears the airway, but always remember to protect that vulnerable neck from spinal injury at the same time.

question: What does the term 'polyspermy' mean?

options.A: Rapid division of cells prior to implantation
options.B: Fertilization of an oocyte by more than one sperm
options.C: The total failure of ovulation to occur in a cycle
options.D: The premature breakdown of the zona pellucida

explanation: Spot on! Polyspermy happens when multiple sperm sneak in, which creates an unstable embryo that cannot survive.

question: Which of these actions is a serious breach of patient confidentiality?

options.A: Asking a mother for her child's immunization history
options.B: Discussing a patient's HIV status with neighbors at the market
options.C: Reporting anonymous malaria totals to the regional health office
options.D: Storing locked physical clinic registers in the facility record room

explanation: Never share private health details outside the clinic! Gossip destroys patient trust and violates professional ethics. What happens in the clinic stays in the clinic.

question: What is the main medication used to treat paragonimiasis?

options.A: Praziquantel
options.B: Chloroquine
options.C: Artemether
options.D: Penicillin

explanation: Spot on! Praziquantel is the go-to anti-worm medication that safely clears out the adult lung flukes.

question: Why do we give zinc supplements to a child with diarrhoea?

options.A: It acts as a strong sedative to help the child sleep
options.B: It shortens the illness duration and repairs gut tissue
options.C: It kills bacteria directly in the stomach lining
options.D: It immediately stops all vomiting within one hour

explanation: Zinc is a helper mineral! It helps the gut lining heal faster, boosts immunity, and cuts down how long the child will suffer from diarrhoea.

question: What is the main goal of evaluating an IEC campaign after it has ended?

options.A: The speed at which the community health extension workers walk
options.B: Whether community knowledge increased and health practices actually changed
options.C: The exact cost of ink used to print the educational leaflets
options.D: How many posters were torn down by heavy rainfall and wind

explanation: Evaluation lets you know if your hard work paid off by checking if people actually learned something new and changed their health habits for the better.

question: What is the big advantage of using rapid molecular tests like GeneXpert for TB?

options.A: They replace the need for taking a thorough patient history.
options.B: They provide fast results and detect drug resistance early.
options.C: They can cure the infection without any medications.
options.D: They are completely painless and require no patient samples.

explanation: GeneXpert is fantastic because it gives results in just a few hours and tells us right away if the drugs won't work against that specific strain.

question: What trouble might a nurse administrator face by ignoring civil service rules and health laws?

options.A: Patients experience faster recovery times due to flexible management
options.B: Staff members become more productive and creative in their duties
options.C: The hospital automatically receives more funding from the federal budget
options.D: The administrator opens the institution and themselves to legal liability

explanation: Operating outside the law is a heavy risk. It can lead to serious legal penalties and lawsuits for both the manager and the hospital. Always best to stick to the guidelines!

question: What is a main duty of a nurse working in a school?

options.A: Purchasing food supplies for the school cafeteria
options.B: Conducting routine health screenings and managing minor injuries
options.C: Setting the financial budget for local education ministries
options.D: Designing the structural blueprints for new school buildings

explanation: Exactly! School nurses focus on first aid, checking students' health, and handling everyday health needs right on campus.

question: Why is open and honest communication with the patient and family crucial after an adverse event?

options.A: It acknowledges what happened with honesty and helps preserve clinical trust
options.B: It legally transfers all responsibility for recovery to the family members
options.C: It guarantees that no formal incident reports will ever be required
options.D: It prevents the patient from receiving any further medical treatments

explanation: Well done! Being transparent with patients and families builds trust and helps everyone heal emotionally after an unexpected medical mistake.

question: Which blood product is best to give a patient who is bleeding heavily because they lack clotting factors?

options.A: 5% Dextrose in water
options.B: Normal Saline solution
options.C: Fresh Frozen Plasma
options.D: Packed Red Blood Cells

explanation: Fresh Frozen Plasma is packed with the vital clotting factors needed to help stop bleeding. You're building great clinical judgment!

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of Cushing's triad when the brainstem is squeezed?

options.A: Irregular breathing patterns
options.B: Persistent tachycardia with rapid weak pulses
options.C: Bradycardia
options.D: Widening pulse pressure

explanation: Cushing's triad features a slow heart rate (bradycardia), not tachycardia, along with a wide pulse pressure and weird breathing patterns.

question: What is a major long-term risk for patients dealing with ongoing autoimmune inflammation and immunosuppression?

options.A: Increased risk of cardiovascular disease and infections
options.B: Complete regeneration of destroyed organ tissue
options.C: Permanent stabilization of normal blood pressure
options.D: Total immunity against all forms of cancer

explanation: Constant inflammation wears down blood vessels over time, and medicines that lower immunity leave patients more open to infections.

question: Why is teamwork between a dietitian and a pharmacist so important for patient safety?

options.A: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital meal trays
options.B: To determine when the patient is ready for hospital discharge
options.C: To decide which nurse will feed the patient during the shift
options.D: To prevent bad interactions between food and prescribed drugs

explanation: Certain foods can block or dangerously increase how medications work, making a joint review by dietitians and pharmacists super important.

question: Which facilities typically represent the tertiary level of health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Primary health care dispensaries in rural villages
options.B: Local government maternity and immunization posts
options.C: Private neighborhood patent medicine shops
options.D: Teaching hospitals and specialist medical centers

explanation: Teaching hospitals and specialized federal medical centers provide the highest level of complex tertiary care. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h4)

question: A patient with an NG tube suddenly feels nauseous and bloated. What should you check first?

options.A: Administer a strong oral tablet for pain relief
options.B: Check gastric residual volume and assess tube patency
options.C: Increase the speed of the tube feeding pump immediately
options.D: Pull the entire tube out right away without checking

explanation: Nausea and bloating usually mean the food isn't draining or emptying properly. Checking how much fluid is left in the stomach (residuals) and making sure the tube isn't clogged is your best first step.

question: A ward manager notices seasonal malaria admissions double every rainy season. What is the best way to use this information?

options.A: Plan ahead to bring in extra temporary staff during rainy months
options.B: Close the ward entirely until the rainy season passes
options.C: Wait until the ward is full and panic
options.D: Reduce nursing shifts to save money for equipment

explanation: Looking at historical trends helps managers forecast busy periods and prepare staff numbers in advance. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why must used needles and medical waste be disposed of with extreme care in a disaster camp?

options.A: To provide building materials for temporary shelters
options.B: To make the garbage bags look neat and tidy
options.C: To keep the air smelling fresh for the residents
options.D: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and biological contamination

explanation: Throwing sharps around carelessly can easily injure children playing nearby or fellow health workers. Safety first, always!

question: Why are newborn babies and burn patients at higher risk of chemical absorption from skin antiseptics?

options.A: Their skin barrier is immature or damaged, allowing greater chemical absorption.
options.B: They are allergic to all known chemical disinfectants in the hospital.
options.C: Their body temperature causes the antiseptics to boil on contact.
options.D: They produce natural enzymes that turn antiseptics into dangerous poisons.

explanation: Spot on! Delicate baby skin or open burn wounds lack that tough outer layer that normally stops chemicals from sinking into the bloodstream.

question: In some traditional settings, why are eggs and chicken meat sometimes withheld from young children?

options.A: Lack of available cooking oil in rural markets
options.B: Strict government laws against eating farm birds
options.C: Fear of causing speech delays, greed, or stubbornness
options.D: Belief that poultry meat causes high blood pressure

explanation: It's a common local myth! Elders sometimes worry that letting kids eat chicken or eggs will make them greedy or delay their talking. As nurses, we gently educate against this.

question: A nurse notices morning shift surgical patients report less pain than evening ones. Why is this a good research problem?

options.A: It highlights a noticeable pattern and potential gap in pain management routines
options.B: It proves that evening nurses are performing their duties incorrectly
options.C: It guarantees a promotion for the nurse who records the observation
options.D: It eliminates the need to administer prescribed pain medications

explanation: Spotting differences in patient care across shifts points to a real clinical puzzle worth investigating. You're thinking like a true researcher!

question: Why are electronic monitors so helpful when looking after unstable patients?

options.A: They make writing shift notes completely unnecessary
options.B: They catch small downward trends before a full crisis hits
options.C: They prevent any sudden changes from ever occurring
options.D: They stop false alarms from ever happening

explanation: Continuous tracking shows tiny shifts in a patient's stability long before a normal manual check would pick them up. Great clinical thinking!

question: Why is it important to monitor pressure and volume during mechanical ventilation?

options.A: It controls the exact body temperature of the patient
options.B: It means you never have to listen to breath sounds with a stethoscope
options.C: It guarantees the patient will be off the machine by morning
options.D: It ensures the machine supports breathing safely without injuring the lungs

explanation: Tracking pressures helps prevent lung damage (barotrauma) while making sure the patient gets enough oxygen. Safety first!

question: Why is studying maternal morbidity just as crucial as looking at maternal mortality?

options.A: Morbidity data is much easier to collect in rural hospitals than mortality numbers
options.B: Mortality rates have dropped to zero globally, making morbidity the only priority
options.C: It focuses solely on the health status of the newborn baby after delivery
options.D: It highlights the hidden burden of long-term suffering and disability survivors face

explanation: For every woman who sadly passes away, many more live with severe, lifelong health issues from pregnancy complications. Understanding this helps us provide better care for mothers in our communities!

question: How should you talk to a parent who is scared about vaccines because of community rumors?

options.A: Tell the parent that asking questions about modern medicine is illegal
options.B: Scold the parent publicly to discourage other community members from doubting
options.C: Listen respectfully, validate their concerns, and provide clear factual explanations
options.D: Ignore the questions entirely and administer the injections without speaking

explanation: As a nurse, patience is key. Listening without judgment and sharing gentle, honest facts builds trust way faster than arguing.

question: How long should a patient rest quietly before having their blood pressure measured?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: At least 5 minutes
options.C: No rest is needed
options.D: At least 1 hour

explanation: A short resting period ensures that recent physical activity or rushing does not falsely elevate the blood pressure reading. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h3)

question: Why is skilled care so important for an elderly patient just leaving the hospital?

options.A: To replace the need for any future primary care physician visits.
options.B: To prevent minor clinical changes from turning into severe health emergencies.
options.C: To ensure the patient never returns to their personal home.
options.D: To completely eliminate all forms of physical therapy.

explanation: Spotting small health changes early is what skilled nursing is all about! It keeps our patients stable and out of trouble. Well done!

question: Why is it so important for the body to keep producing hCG right after the embryo implants?

options.A: It directly softens the pelvic bones to prepare for eventual childbirth
options.B: It stimulates the fetal heart to begin beating inside the gestational sac
options.C: It forces the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone and prevents menstruation
options.D: It stops the maternal immune system from ever recognizing the fetus

explanation: Spot on! hCG sends a vital signal to keep progesterone flowing, which stops the womb lining from shedding so the pregnancy can continue safely.

question: What is the main thing that separates a true experiment from a quasi-experiment?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of statistical testing
options.B: The use of patient interviews for data collection
options.C: The presence of a clinical nurse researcher
options.D: Random assignment of participants to groups

explanation: You nailed it! True experiments use random chance (like flipping a coin) to drop people into different groups, while quasi-experiments don't use strict random mixing. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h4)

question: An infection control nurse sees more wound infections popping up on a surgical ward. What should be the first step?

options.A: Close the entire hospital building permanently without telling anyone
options.B: Stop washing hands between patients to build natural immunity
options.C: Prescribe the strongest available antibiotic to every single visitor
options.D: Collect and culture samples from suspected sources to identify the causative organism

explanation: Correct! Culturing samples helps track down the root cause of an outbreak so the healthcare team can stop it in its tracks.

question: Why must you wash off blood and dirt before putting a disinfectant on a surface?

options.A: Organic matter shields the microorganisms and blocks the chemical from working.
options.B: Blood mixes with the disinfectant to create a pleasant scent.
options.C: Blood changes the color of the disinfectant so it looks clean.
options.D: Organic matter makes the disinfectant evaporate too slowly.

explanation: Correct! Blood and body fluids can hide germs and block the disinfectant from reaching them. Always clean first, then disinfect!

question: What is the main reason for doing a tracheotomy?

options.A: To bypass the lungs during severe pneumonia
options.B: To prevent food from entering the esophagus
options.C: To permanently remove the need for oxygen therapy
options.D: To create a direct opening into the trachea

explanation: A tracheotomy is simply a surgical opening made right into the trachea to give the patient an alternative airway. You've got this!

question: A patient on IV quinine for severe malaria reports dizziness and ringing in the ears. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assume this is a normal side effect and document it routinely
options.B: Notify the prescriber and evaluate for signs of quinine toxicity
options.C: Stop the intravenous line permanently without telling anyone
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water

explanation: Spot on! These are classic signs of cinchonism (quinine toxicity). The doctor must be informed right away to keep the patient safe.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when designing a community mental health intervention?

options.A: Using respectful and accessible local language
options.B: Imposing a rigid foreign program without consulting local leaders
options.C: Involving local community members in creating program content
options.D: Designing activities that fit the cultural context

explanation: Imposing programs without local consultation ignores cultural realities and almost always leads to poor community participation and failure. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is a quiet environment important when conducting a neurological assessment?

options.A: To prevent the hospital equipment from malfunctioning
options.B: To keep the patient fast asleep throughout the examination
options.C: To ensure the lighting remains perfectly dim at all times
options.D: To accurately evaluate mental status, speech, and cranial nerves

explanation: Excessive background noise can distract the patient or mask subtle speech and hearing abnormalities. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is a very common result of high humidity inside an oxygen tent?

options.A: Water condensation building up on the inner plastic walls
options.B: Sudden dropping of the room's overall humidity level
options.C: Freezing of the oxygen gas into solid ice crystals
options.D: Complete drying out of the patient's nasal passages

explanation: All that moisture in the enclosed space naturally turns into water droplets on the cooler plastic walls of the tent.

question: A distressed family member is upset because their dying relative refuses to eat meals. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Scold the patient for not trying hard enough to maintain their body weight
options.B: Tell the family to force feed the patient large portions using a syringe
options.C: Explain that declining appetite is a natural part of the illness and focus on mouth care
options.D: Insist that the doctor order total parenteral nutrition immediately

explanation: Reassuring the family and shifting attention away from forced feeding reduces anxiety for everyone involved. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h5)

question: Why should a performance review session be a two-way conversation?

options.A: It speeds up the meeting so everyone can return to patient care faster
options.B: It legally prevents the nurse from ever receiving a low grade
options.C: It ensures the manager does not have to prepare any written notes
options.D: It allows the nurse to share their perspective and explain workplace challenges

explanation: An appraisal shouldn't be a lecture! When you get to share your side, your manager can understand the real challenges you face on the ward.

question: What surgical approach accesses the fistula tract through the vaginal wall?

options.A: Transanal repair
options.B: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
options.C: Transvaginal repair
options.D: Abdominal resection

explanation: The transvaginal approach directly exposes and closes the defect through the posterior wall of the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: What happens inside a bone when a tumor starts growing in it?

options.A: Normal bone remodeling balance is disrupted, leading to weakened bone integrity
options.B: Calcium is rapidly absorbed back into the matrix, making bones harder
options.C: Bone marrow production shuts down permanently without affecting bone strength
options.D: The bone responds by producing extra thick layers of solid cortical bone

explanation: Tumors mess up the normal building and breaking down process of bones, leaving them fragile. Great job keeping this in mind!

question: Why do we sometimes treat a dry, hacking cough with medicine, even though coughing is a natural body defense?

options.A: It prevents oxygen from reaching the brain tissues.
options.B: It stops the heart from beating too fast during sleep.
options.C: It always indicates a permanent lung collapse.
options.D: It causes tiredness and chest pain without bringing up any phlegm.

explanation: A dry cough doesn't help clear anything out—it just leaves your patient exhausted and sore. Treating it helps them get some much-needed rest!

question: A patient on hydrochlorothiazide complains of feeling very weak and dizzy. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink less water throughout the day
options.B: Discontinue the medication immediately without consulting the doctor
options.C: Check the most recent serum electrolyte laboratory results
options.D: Instruct the patient to increase daily dietary table salt intake

explanation: Well reasoned! Weakness and dizziness can mean electrolytes are out of whack. Always check the lab results to see what's happening with potassium and sodium.

question: A patient is nearly ready for independent life and only needs short-term guidance on budgeting and job hunting. Which facility fits best?

options.A: Transitional living facility
options.B: Long-term nursing home
options.C: Maximum security asylum
options.D: Acute psychiatric ward

explanation: You nailed it! Transitional facilities are short-term setups designed to help patients brush up on practical skills like managing money and finding jobs before they head out on their own.

question: Administrative nursing informatics is primarily used for which of the following tasks?

options.A: Administering intravenous medications directly to patients
options.B: Managing staffing schedules, budgets, and operational metrics
options.C: Designing interactive smartphone apps for general public use
options.D: Conducting laboratory experiments on cellular disease models

explanation: Nurse leaders use administrative tools to oversee hospital operations, staffing levels, and financial or quality metrics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why are congregate living settings like nursing homes particularly vulnerable to disease outbreaks?

options.A: The complete absence of handwashing sinks
options.B: The high rate of sudden resident discharges
options.C: The requirement for outdoor recreational sports
options.D: The close proximity of medically frail residents

explanation: Correct! When vulnerable people live close together, germs can spread fast unless we are super strict with our infection control.

question: What is the main job of the 'memory cells' created when someone gets vaccinated?

options.A: To permanently alter the person's genetic DNA structure
options.B: To destroy healthy tissue to make space for white blood cells
options.C: To slow down the immune response to prevent inflammation
options.D: To provide a rapid and strong defense upon future exposure to the germ

explanation: Exactly! Memory cells never forget a face; they spot the real germ later in life and fight it off instantly.

question: What does the term 'fidelity' mean when talking about healthcare simulators?

options.A: How easily the simulator can be moved between classrooms
options.B: How closely the simulation mimics a real-life clinical situation
options.C: How much the simulator costs to purchase and maintain
options.D: How many students can use the simulator at the same time

explanation: Fidelity describes the level of realism and how well the simulation copies actual patient care scenarios. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why would a doctor choose an MRI over a standard X-ray for a patient?

options.A: MRIs can be done easily with any metal implants present
options.B: MRIs are much cheaper and faster to perform in emergencies
options.C: MRIs do not require any patient preparation or screening
options.D: MRIs provide much clearer images of soft tissues and organs

explanation: Standard X-rays are great for bones, but an MRI is far superior for showing details inside muscles, brains, ligaments, and organs. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which human factor frequently causes industrial accidents in the workplace?

options.A: Strict adherence to international building codes
options.B: Regular maintenance of old electrical grids
options.C: Operator fatigue and bypassed safety checks
options.D: Excessive routine safety training for workers

explanation: Well done! When workers are exhausted or skip safety rules to save time, accidents are much more likely to happen.

question: Why do we irrigate a fresh bite wound with plenty of sterile fluid?

options.A: To dissolve all the surrounding dead skin cells
options.B: To physically wash away bacteria and loose debris
options.C: To permanently freeze the nerve endings to stop pain
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of new blood cells

explanation: Using fluid force is one of our best nursing tools to physically rinse out contaminating microbes and dirt left behind by the bite.

question: Which popular local dietary combination is most famous for triggering painful gout attacks?

options.A: Fresh green vegetables
options.B: Low-fat dairy products
options.C: Beer and red meat
options.D: Citrus fruits and juices

explanation: Correct! Red meat and alcoholic drinks like beer are packed with purines, which quickly turn into uric acid and can spark a flare-up.

question: Why does a good safety culture discourage hiding clinical mistakes?

options.A: Because nurses who make mistakes must be immediately suspended
options.B: Because patients always find out the truth through their medical records
options.C: Because hospital management requires public reports for every small incident
options.D: Because hiding errors prevents the team from learning and stopping repeat events

explanation: When staff feel safe reporting mistakes, the institution can analyze what went wrong and fix the system to protect future patients. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h1)

question: In the human female reproductive tract, where does fertilization usually happen?

options.A: Surface of the ovary
options.B: Lower third of the uterine cavity
options.C: Ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.D: Cervical canal

explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle section of the fallopian tube and provides the perfect meeting place for the swimming sperm and the released egg.

question: Why must you store your interview audio files and transcripts in password-protected digital folders?

options.A: To prevent accidental loss of data and protect patient confidentiality
options.B: To speed up the internet connection in the research office
options.C: To make the files look more professional for publishing
options.D: To allow the general public to read private hospital stories

explanation: Exactly right! Patient stories are deeply personal, and keeping digital files secure is a core part of ethical nursing practice.

question: Roughly how many extra daily calories does a breastfeeding mother need?

options.A: 1000 to 1200 kilocalories
options.B: Zero extra calories are needed
options.C: 450 to 500 kilocalories
options.D: 100 to 150 kilocalories

explanation: Making breast milk takes a lot of body power! Mums actually need even more extra energy daily while breastfeeding than they did while pregnant.

question: What should be a nurse's main focus when giving diet advice to a low-income family?

options.A: Advising them to eat only once every two days
options.B: Recommending affordable, locally available foods
options.C: Telling them to stop eating traditional family meals
options.D: Insisting they purchase expensive imported vitamins

explanation: Good nutrition advice has to be practical. Always recommend foods that the family can easily find and afford in their local market.

question: How does disease surveillance differ from standard bedside nursing care?

options.A: Surveillance is only performed by doctors inside specialized laboratories
options.B: Surveillance deals exclusively with chronic genetic disorders
options.C: Surveillance requires advanced surgical skills instead of basic bedside observation
options.D: Surveillance focuses on population-level health trends rather than single patients

explanation: While bedside nursing cares for one patient at a time, surveillance looks at the big picture to protect entire communities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why should a community health nurse look at the health needs of a whole group instead of just single patients?

options.A: It helps allocate resources effectively to design meaningful programs
options.B: It guarantees complete eradication of all chronic diseases
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever visit individual households
options.D: It ensures every single citizen receives specialized surgery

explanation: Looking at the big picture helps you focus on what really plagues the population so you can put your limited time and materials to the best possible use!

question: Why are women more likely to get bladder infections than men?

options.A: The female bladder lacks any form of transitional epithelial lining
options.B: Women produce significantly less urine volume over a 24-hour period
options.C: The female urethra is much shorter and closer to the anal opening
options.D: The female trigone is larger and traps bacteria much more easily

explanation: Anatomy plays a big role here! The female urethra is only about four centimeters long, giving outside bacteria a short and easy path straight into the bladder.

question: What type of heat loss happens when a baby is laid directly on a cold, unheated examination table?

options.A: Conduction
options.B: Convection
options.C: Radiation
options.D: Evaporation

explanation: Conduction is heat loss through direct contact—like when a warm baby touches a cold surface. Always remember to use a warm blanket on that table!

question: What is a normal and harmless effect of rifampin that nurses should warn patients about?

options.A: Bright green coloration of saliva and fingernails
options.B: Permanent yellow tinting of the skin and eye sclera
options.C: Orange-red discoloration of urine, sweat, and tears
options.D: Severe darkening of the skin on the hands and feet

explanation: Rifampin naturally dyes body fluids a reddish-orange color. It looks alarming, but it's completely normal and harmless!

question: In infection control, what do we mean by the 'source of infection'?

options.A: The specific place or object from which an infectious agent passes to a host
options.B: Any medication used to treat a bacterial disease
options.C: The permanent habitat where a microorganism always multiplies
options.D: The specific immune response mounted by a healthy patient

explanation: Think of the source as the direct hand-off point—it's where the germ jumps from to land on the patient. You've got this!

question: How does SIMV (Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation) differ from Assist-Control mode?

options.A: SIMV delivers breaths only when the patient makes zero respiratory effort
options.B: SIMV allows spontaneous breaths between mandatory machine breaths without extra volume support
options.C: SIMV is only used for patients who are paralyzed or heavily sedated
options.D: SIMV completely controls every single breath the patient takes without exception

explanation: SIMV gives the patient a bit of freedom! The machine gives scheduled breaths, but in between those, the patient can take their own natural breaths without the machine forcing extra air.

question: What is the main building block your body uses to make all female sex hormones?

options.A: Cholesterol
options.B: Amino acids
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Triglycerides

explanation: Think of cholesterol as the parent molecule! Without it, the body couldn't build vital steroid hormones like estrogen and progesterone. You've got this!

question: Which clinical observation around the umbilical stump indicates the development of omphalitis?

options.A: Redness of the skin and foul-smelling discharge
options.B: A dry, black, and completely shriveled stump
options.C: Natural separation of the cord after one week
options.D: A small drop of clear blood upon diaper removal

explanation: Spreading redness, swelling, and pus or bad smells around the navel are classic signs of a dangerous umbilical infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h5)

question: How do nurses commonly use mobile handheld devices in modern hospitals?

options.A: To scan patient ID bands and medication barcodes at the bedside
options.B: To play streaming music videos in patient rooms
options.C: To make personal phone calls during quiet night shifts
options.D: To take photographs of hospital visitors for security passes

explanation: Bedside scanners are a nurse's best friend for safety, helping ensure the right medication always reaches the right patient.

question: Why do we run lab tests and checks for patients in the intensive care unit (ICU)?

options.A: To replace the standard physical assessment entirely
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays
options.C: To track how well current treatments are working
options.D: To shorten the nursing shift handover time

explanation: Think of lab tests and diagnostics as your patient's report card. They give us real-time clues to see if our care is helping or if things are taking a turn.

question: How does having a larger risk pool help a health insurance scheme?

options.A: It balances out the costs between healthy and sick members more effectively
options.B: It ensures that taxes are completely abolished
options.C: It removes the need for patients to ever visit a pharmacy
options.D: It allows the hospital to hire foreign doctors exclusively

explanation: The more healthy people join the pool, the easier it is to cover the medical bills of the few who fall sick. Safety truly lies in numbers!

question: What primary role does the family unit play in the food supply chain?

options.A: It acts as the final link that consumes and utilizes the food.
options.B: It regulates international trade agreements for agricultural goods.
options.C: It determines large-scale industrial farming methods.
options.D: It sets global market prices for staple crops.

explanation: Families sit at the end of the supply chain, turning raw food into meals and nutrition for household members. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h1)

question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding for a healthy newborn?

options.A: Until the first tooth appears
options.B: First two weeks of life
options.C: First six months of life
options.D: First twelve months of life

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding provides all necessary nutrients and antibodies without needing water or other foods for the first six months. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h5)

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease shows signs of metabolic acidosis. What lab result would a nurse expect to see?

options.A: An elevated blood pH well above 7.45
options.B: An increased respiratory rate causing carbon dioxide retention
options.C: A high concentration of bicarbonate in the fresh urine
options.D: A low serum bicarbonate level on the lab report

explanation: Spot on! Metabolic acidosis means the body is low on its main buffer, so you'll see a drop in serum bicarbonate levels on the patient's lab results.

question: Which of these is a natural disaster?

options.A: A structural bridge collapse
options.B: A major factory chemical leak
options.C: An industrial nuclear meltdown
options.D: A volcanic eruption

explanation: Volcanic eruptions happen naturally from the earth, while chemical leaks and bridge collapses are caused by human activities or broken structures. Simple and clear!

question: Which goal of health spending focuses specifically on making sure poor and vulnerable citizens are not left out?

options.A: Quality assurance
options.B: Cost containment
options.C: Equity
options.D: Privatization

explanation: Think of equity as fairness. It ensures that healthcare resources reach everyone, especially those with lower incomes.

question: What do we call unintended and harmful responses to a medication given at normal, standard doses?

options.A: Primary drug actions
options.B: Placebo responses
options.C: Therapeutic plateaus
options.D: Adverse drug reactions

explanation: Even when we give the right dose, bodies can react unpredictably. Adverse drug reactions are those unwanted, harmful side effects we always watch out for.

question: Why does the ventral respiratory group kick in when someone starts exercising hard?

options.A: To slow down the breathing rate and conserve energy
options.B: To drive forceful exhalation and deeper breaths required by the exertion
options.C: To bypass the damaged pons and restore normal speech
options.D: To cool down the brainstem through rapid airflow

explanation: Quiet breathing is mostly about inhaling, but heavy exercise requires extra effort. That's when the ventral group steps in to help you breathe out forcefully.

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when responding to a cardiac arrest in a patient with skull traction?

options.A: Keeping the neck in neutral alignment during all emergency maneuvers
options.B: Ensuring a doctor or emergency team member manages the head position
options.C: Removing the traction weights immediately to start chest compressions
options.D: Following hospital guidelines for emergency airway management

question: Why do nurses need to triage patients when the emergency department is packed?

question: Why are simulation labs so helpful for nursing students in training?

question: A young student newly diagnosed with PCOS feels very upset about her acne and irregular periods. What is the best initial nursing response?

options.B: Explain that psychological stress has no connection to physical hormones

question: Why is simple bed making considered an essential clinical nursing skill rather than just housekeeping?

options.C: It directly promotes patient comfort, safety, and skin integrity

question: What happens if a research question is unclear or confusing?

question: If a brain tumor starts growing inside the skull, what has to happen first to keep pressure from rising too high?

question: Why is putting a child in an orphanage usually considered a last resort?

options.A: Extended family members refuse to let children visit orphanages
options.B: Family-based care is better for a child's emotional development
options.C: Orphanages are illegal under Nigerian federal health laws
options.D: Institutions only accept children who are over eighteen years old

question: What causes the glandular tissue of the breast to shrink after menopause?

options.D: Blockage of the lactiferous ducts

question: How does the way a baby is born affect their early microbiome?

question: A school clinic notices a sudden jump in waterborne infections among students. What should the team do next?

options.C: Punish the students for failing to wash their hands at home

question: Why is it important for researchers to discuss study limitations during data interpretation?

question: What is a core responsibility of a nurse working at a mass gathering?

question: Besides relieving pressure, what is another major reason for doing a paracentesis?

question: Why does losing a massive amount of blood lead straight into shock?

options.C: The heart beats too slowly to pump blood to the lungs

question: Which of these items belongs specifically in the pathological waste category?

question: How does health insurance help protect patients from poverty?

options.B: By ensuring all hospitals are built in rural farming areas
options.C: By making every medical procedure completely free of cost

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for patients with inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: To achieve a complete cure of the genetic mutation
options.B: To stop the natural progression of the disease entirely
options.C: To reverse the physical breakdown of body tissues
options.D: To maximize remaining function and quality of life

question: What natural body process helps the uterus contract and shrink back down after delivery?

question: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened (but still alive) version of a germ?

question: A nursing student is teaching a patient how to track her fertile window. Which recommendation gives the most accurate tracking?

options.A: Checking basal body temperature to predict ovulation ahead of time

options.C: Relying solely on a standard 28-day calendar calculation

question: Which brain chemical is severely lacking in Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Acetylcholine

question: What main feature defines a traditional community in public health?

question: What is caregiver burnout?

options.A: An allergic reaction to cleaning supplies used in the home

options.C: A sudden medical illness caught from a patient in the hospital

question: Which of these is a key step for nursing leaders building a Just Culture?

question: A junior nurse makes a minor error while trying a new wound care dressing. What response shows true psychological safety?

question: A patient takes a bitter drug. Which family of receptors on their tongue will most likely detect that bitterness?

question: Which macronutrient requires the most energy for the body to digest and process?

question: How can you, as a bedside nurse, help improve injection safety standards in your clinic?

question: Why do patients with endocarditis need to take antibiotics for many weeks instead of just a few days?

question: Why does the pregnant body develop natural insulin resistance in the later stages of gestation?

question: If a patient is stable and suddenly starts getting worse during an ABCDEF check, what should the team do right away?

question: How does the Contributory Pension Scheme work for nursing personnel in the public sector?

question: What is a confounding variable in research?

question: How are wearable health trackers beginning to influence professional health records?

question: Why do some families continue to practice FGM despite legal bans?

question: Your clinic has limited funds and staff. How should you decide which health problem to tackle first?

question: Following a sudden pipeline explosion, a hospital receives dozens of patients with severe burns. What immediate care will these patients need most?

question: Why is teaching family caregivers a key part of subacute discharge planning?

question: A toddler arrives at the emergency unit suddenly drooling, making high-pitched breathing sounds (stridor), and very restless, but has no cough. What should you do first?

question: Why should nurse researchers use both traditional and modern ways to share their work?

question: Why do we need clear referral pathways from community clinics up to Tier 4 specialists?

question: What is a recommended nursing intervention to help prevent post-dural puncture headaches?

question: What is a major social reason why communities practice food taboos?

question: What is the ultimate goal of interpreting research data in nursing?

question: Why must nurses wear personal protective equipment (PPE) during a hazardous material spill?

question: What is the main job of smallholder farmers in local food systems?

question: Why does severe peripheral vascular disease often lead to an amputation?

question: What is the best way to greet a client who has missed several family planning appointments?

question: Which of these everyday habits helps drive antibiotic resistance in our communities?

question: What is point prevalence?

options.B: Predicting how long a chronic illness will last
